title: Pre-Analysis — Forward Engine Mount Bolt Bushing Standard on CVX-7200
abstract: Closed pre-analysis for the introduction of a bushing standard in the forward engine mount bolt bores on CVX-7200 installations, covering the bore inspection, the mount part list and the pylon access sequence.

sections.objective: Establish the documentation impact of bushing the forward engine mount bolt bores on the CVX-7200 installation, and confirm that the change can be confined to that engine type without any consequence for the Auran installation, which shares the pylon and part of the access. The order was raised by the powerplant integration office after bore wear findings at the first heavy checks on the highest utilisation aircraft, and had to close before the engine build standard was frozen for the year.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and one of them gates the release. The detailed and eddy current inspection of the bolt bore is written against the unbushed bore diameter throughout, in the probe selection, the reference block and the acceptance limits, and every one of those has to change for a bushed bore. Left as it is, the task would report a bushed bore as worn beyond limits on the first inspection after embodiment. The mount and heat shield figure needs the bushing and its retaining ring as new items with an engine type effectivity, since the same figure serves both installations. The third item came from the zone overlap alone: the oil filter housing removal uses the same pylon access and the bushing installation tooling occupies that envelope for most of a shift.
sections.next_steps: Release was authorised with the inspection task reissue as the only gating condition. The parts list change was scheduled with the modification. The line maintenance office was asked to sequence the bushing installation and any oil filter housing work in the same pylon opening rather than in consecutive shifts, and the note was added to the accomplishment instructions of the retrofit bulletin when it was drafted.

similarity_seeds: bolt bore wear at a forward engine mount
bushing installation to restore a worn fitting bore

tasks.title: Search mount and pylon data across both engine installations
Check the inspection reference block and limits against a bushed bore
Review the pylon access sequence with line maintenance

expected_findings.rationale: The probe selection, the reference block and the acceptance limits are all stated against the unbushed bore diameter. On a bushed bore the same inspection returns an indication at the bush interface and the published limit would condemn a serviceable mount at the first check after embodiment.
expected_findings.resolution: Reissue the task with a bushed bore procedure, a new reference block and limits stated per bore standard. This gates the modification release.

evidence.similarity_note: The figure and the modification name the same mount, heat shield and attachment hardware in the same words, so the figure is retrieved by either pass.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure serves both engine installations from one illustration. The bushing and its retaining ring have to be added with an engine type effectivity, or a Auran operator will order parts that do not belong on the aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the two items with an engine type effectivity note and repeat the note in the figure preamble.

expected_findings.rationale: Found through the pylon zones alone; the two documents have no vocabulary in common. The oil filter housing removal opens the same pylon panels, and the bushing installation tooling occupies that envelope for most of a shift, so the two cannot be run in parallel on the same engine.
expected_findings.resolution: Sequence the two in one pylon opening and record the note in the accomplishment instructions of the retrofit bulletin.

type_data.conclusion: Issued 2018-10-16. One gating inspection reissue, one parts list change and one access sequencing note. Cleared to proceed once the inspection task is republished.
